```{=latex}
\giLandscapeChapterOpener{A Landscape-Only Chapter}
\begin{landscape}
\giLandscapeChapterHeader
```

This whole chapter is landscape, and it starts with no wasted
portrait page — no bare title sitting alone before the actual
content begins. Compare this to a normal chapter with an *embedded*
landscape table (like Chapter 1): here, the chapter title itself
shows horizontally, as part of the landscape page's own running
header, instead of on a separate portrait page first.

```{=latex}
\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.2\linewidth}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.2\linewidth}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.2\linewidth}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.2\linewidth}
@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\rowcolor{giTableHeaderShade}
\textbf{Column A} & \textbf{Column B} & \textbf{Column C} & \textbf{Column D} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\cellcolor{giTableFirstColShade}Row 1 & Data & Data & Data \\
\bottomrule
\caption{\label{tbl-landscape-chapter-example}A table inside a landscape-only chapter.}
\end{longtable}
```

This is the pattern to reach for whenever a whole chapter's content
is naturally wide — a large data table, a wide diagram, anything
that doesn't fit a portrait column at a readable size.

```{=latex}
\giLandscapeFooter
\end{landscape}
```

```{=latex}
% \giEnableAppendix needs to fire before the NEXT chapter's heading,
% not after — same "content before a heading gets reordered" rule
% covered in the README. This file is now the last numbered chapter
% before the appendix starts, so this switch lives at its true end.
\giEnableAppendix
```
